sources.name: Unicode Standard Annex #9: Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm

provenance.notes: Written in this phase from the cited references and re-expressed; the Arabic text is the researcher's own wording and needs a native reviewer. The checks are proposals for the harness, not yet run.

title.ar: المؤشر والتحديد من المنصة لا من رسمنا
title.en: Caret and selection come from the platform, not from our drawing

statement.ar: في الحقول النصية اترك حركة المؤشر والتحديد والحذف للمتصفح. لا ترسم مؤشرًا أو تحديدًا مخصصًا، ولا تحسب المواضع بعدد المحارف. أي معالجة للقيمة أثناء الكتابة تحفظ موضع المؤشر بوحدات العناقيد.
statement.en: In text fields leave caret movement, selection and deletion to the browser. Do not draw a custom caret or selection and do not compute positions by counting characters. Any processing of the value while typing preserves the caret position in grapheme-cluster units.

rationale.ar: في النص المختلط التحديد المنطقي المتصل يظهر بصريًا قطعتين، والمؤشر له موضعان عند حد الاتجاه. والحذف الخلفي في العربية يزيل آخر علامة تشكيل أولًا. إعادة تنفيذ ذلك تنتج أخطاء لا تُحصى.
rationale.en: In mixed text a contiguous logical selection is visually two pieces, and the caret has two positions at a direction boundary. Backspace in Arabic removes the last mark first. Re-implementing this yields endless errors.

checks: No field component renders its own caret or selection element.
After an input transformation (digit conversion, space replacement) the caret is after the same grapheme as before; verified by typing in the middle of each text-stress and amounts string.
Deleting from the end of text-stress TS-050 with Backspace removes one code point per press until the base letter (platform behaviour is not intercepted).
Selection APIs are called with UTF-16 offsets that lie on grapheme boundaries.
